title: Inquest rules police shooting justified
article: A B.C. coroner's inquest in Kamloops this week has dispelled most of the questions Rhonda Lelek had about the death of her son. But one remains.
Lelek listened to testimony from witnesses who said her son Graham Maryancik attacked RCMP Const. Rob Romanuik, who later shot and killed Maryancik at a roadside turnout May 26, 2004.
But while she agreed with the five-member jury that the officer was justified in his action, she can't figure out why her son would attack the police officer in the first place.

"When the cop spoke, he was visibly shaken and his voice was crackling," Lelek said. "I don't know, to try and look at it from both sides -if everything they said was true then (the officer) feared for his life."

Maryancik once called Kelowna home, though that isn't the proudest moment for him or his family because he was arrested with four others when police took down Kelowna's first crystal meth lab in 2001.

He was on his way to Kelowna to deal with the charges when he left his fiancee and infant son in Revelstoke in 2004. His plan was to drive to Kelowna that night to be ready for court in the morning. Instead, he was about an hour from where he should have been when he drove his rented minivan into a rest stop at Craigellachie and side- swiped two vehicles before landing in a ditch filled with water.
He was acting very strangely, according to a witness who helped him out of his van, trying desperately to give away his ring, a family heirloom.
Police officers arrived and spoke with Maryancik. Romanuik asked him to return to his vehicle to get his identification and registration.
But when Maryancik returned, he surprised the officer, threw him down and began beating him.
The officer managed to hit Maryancik twice with a large flashlight but it had no effect. The officer then fired two shots, hitting Maryancik in the hand and then in the neck, killing him.
Toxicology results showed nothing in Maryancik's system that might explain his actions.
Lelek and her family believe her son was trying to straighten out his life, particularly since his child, Cole, was born.
She said Maryancik had expected the criminal charges against him would be dropped on his visit to Kelowna.
The coroner's jury found Maryancik's death was accidental, that the use of force was justified and it had no recommendations about how to avoid similar deaths.
Lelek said she was satisfied there was nothing more to the death of her son.
"I had to see and hear the witnesses, just to see if it was believable to me or not and it was," she said.
"The cop seemed believable. I jus don't know what caused (my son) to do that."
